data.standardized_narrative: At 1 January 2019 the Syndicate's gross claims outstanding (claims reserves) stood at GBP 830.4m. The report does not disclose a single aggregate GROSS prioryear development number; the 2017 Year of Account was reinsured to close into 2018 (RITC premium GBP 219.3m) and closed at the end of 2019 with a loss (2.71% of capacity), which distorts development comparators. The Syndicate highlights material gross exposures to a number of catastrophe events (e.g. Typhoon Hagibis and Faxai in 2019 and Hurricane Michael, Typhoon Jebi, the Camp and Woolsey wildfires and the Lurssen shipyard loss in 2018) with mixed movements by line - some lines (notably Third party liability and parts of casualty/A&H) strengthened, while Property and Marine showed releases in the year-end gross outstanding balances overall.
raw_causal_phrases: The 2017 Year of Account has Reinsured to Close ("RITC") into the Syndicate's 2018 Year of Account for an RITC premium of GBP 219.3m.
Under Lloyd's Accounting rules, the Syndicate's 2017 Year of Account closed at the end of 2019, with a loss of 2.71% of capacity.
The Syndicate has gross material exposure to Typhoon Hagibis and Typhoon Faxai in the 2019 Year of Account.
The net exposure to these losses are immaterial.
Last year, the Syndicate had material exposure to the Hurricane Michael, Typhoon Jebi, the Camp and Woolsey Wildfires and the Lurssen Shipyard loss in the 2018 Year of Account.
During the year, the exposure to Typhoon Jebi and Lurseen Shipyard have deteriorated; however, there has been an improvement for the Camp and Woolsey Wildfires.
The cessions made to SPA 6118 and SPA 6132 by the Syndicate are on a funds withheld basis

data.data_quality_notes: An explicit aggregate GROSS 'movement in prior year's provision for claims outstanding' was not located in the notes. The 2017 RITC into 2018 (RITC premium GBP 219.3m) and closure of the 2017 Year of Account (loss) distort development comparisons and make deriving a reliable aggregated prior-year development figure from the claims development tables unreliable. A gross claims development triangle is present in the notes but its layout and the RITC make automated extraction uncertain; therefore no single prior-year development GBP figure is provided.
